hunks.baseline: Contrary to what I’d expected, the Imperial Palace hadn’t changed much since my first visit. No dramatic transformation or anything.
hunks.sol: I’d expected some dramatic change, but the Imperial Palace looked much the same as it had on my first visit.

hunks.baseline: Palace attendants in neat uniforms hurried back and forth, while the heavily armed Embroidered Uniform Guards stood watch at their posts like iron towers.
hunks.sol: Palace attendants in neat uniforms hurried back and forth, while heavily armed Embroidered Uniform Guards stood watch at their posts like iron towers.

hunks.baseline: But if there was one big change, it was me.
hunks.sol: If anything had changed, it was me.

hunks.baseline: When a group of palace attendants coming from the other direction bowed deeply as they passed, I thought it was just a coincidence.
hunks.sol: When a group of palace attendants approaching from the other direction bowed deeply as they passed, I thought it was a coincidence.

hunks.baseline: Even when the Embroidered Uniform Guards, standing watch with a formidable air, struck their armor and saluted, I didn’t think much of it.
hunks.sol: Even when the Embroidered Uniform Guards struck their armor and saluted, I didn’t think much of it. Jeong Hogun had considerable pull among the Guard, so it seemed only natural that they’d salute him.

hunks.baseline: I just assumed it was because Jeong Hogun—a man with considerable pull even among the Embroidered Uniform Guards—was accompanying me.

hunks.baseline: But Jeong Hogun’s reply to my joking remark was utterly calm.
hunks.sol: Jeong Hogun’s reply to my joking remark was utterly calm.

hunks.baseline: Only then did it hit me.
hunks.sol: Only then did it hit me. Only then did I see it.

hunks.baseline: Only then did I see it.
The gazes of the people passing around us—their eyes filled with gratitude and respect—were fixed solely on me.
hunks.sol: The people passing us were looking at me. The gratitude and respect in their eyes were meant for me alone.

hunks.baseline: I hesitated, at a loss for words, when Jeong Hogun’s steady stride came to an abrupt halt.
hunks.sol: I was still at a loss for words when Jeong Hogun came to an abrupt halt.

hunks.baseline: No—not just his. Everyone who’d come with him stopped at the same time.
hunks.sol: No—not just him. Everyone who’d come with him stopped at the same time.

hunks.baseline: *Clop.*
hunks.sol: *Clank.*

hunks.baseline: With a movement as sharp as a blade, they rang with the heavy sound of metal.
hunks.sol: They moved as one, with a heavy ring of metal.

hunks.baseline: A dozen or so jang away, Jeong Hogun glanced at the plaque that read *Qianqing Palace*, then turned to look at me.
hunks.sol: Jeong Hogun glanced at the plaque reading *Qianqing Palace* a dozen or so jang ahead, then turned to me.

hunks.baseline: “We may not get another chance to see each other, so I should say this now.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know when we’ll see each other again, so I should say this now.”

hunks.baseline: The sharp eyes visible beneath his low-pulled helmet softened in an instant, curving like a crescent moon.
hunks.sol: The sharp eyes beneath his low-pulled helmet softened, curving like a crescent moon.

hunks.baseline: I stared at Jeong Hogun, eyes wide.
hunks.sol: I stared at him, eyes wide.

hunks.baseline: The back that had never bowed to anyone but the Emperor, the stiff neck—both were inclining toward me.
hunks.sol: Jeong Hogun had never bowed to anyone but the Emperor. Now his rigid back and neck inclined toward me as he offered a deeply respectful fist-and-palm salute.

hunks.baseline: Along with a most respectful fist-and-palm salute.
*Ching, ching, ching!*
hunks.sol: *Shing! Shing! Shing!*

hunks.baseline: Dozens of Embroidered Uniform Guards shouted in unison and drew their swords, gripping them in reverse.
hunks.sol: Dozens of Embroidered Uniform Guards echoed him and drew their swords, gripping them in reverse.

hunks.baseline: They stood in two neat rows on either side of the path leading to Qianqing Palace. I couldn’t help but burst out laughing.
hunks.sol: They stood in two neat rows on either side of the path to Qianqing Palace. I couldn’t help laughing.

hunks.baseline: But I stopped laughing almost at once and returned their salute, bringing my hands together.
hunks.sol: But I stopped almost at once and returned their salute.

hunks.baseline: “See you again sometime. We will.”
hunks.sol: “We’ll meet again. We will.”

hunks.baseline: A few words, spoken from the heart.
That was enough.
hunks.sol: I meant it. That was enough.

hunks.baseline: No one knew when we’d meet again, but I decided to leave the rest of the conversation for that day.
hunks.sol: No one knew when we’d meet again. I’d leave everything else until then. Every meeting and every bond came with a parting, after all.

hunks.baseline: Every meeting, every bond, eventually came with a parting.
*Clop. Clop.*
hunks.sol: *Step. Step.*

hunks.baseline: I walked slowly along the path Jeong Hogun and the Embroidered Uniform Guards had made for me.
hunks.sol: I walked slowly down the path Jeong Hogun and the guards had made for me.

hunks.baseline: Beneath the high eaves of Qianqing Palace, the twin armored guards were waiting. A new scar finally let me tell their faces apart.
hunks.sol: Beneath the high eaves of Qianqing Palace, the twin armed guards were waiting. Thanks to a new scar, I could finally tell their faces apart.

hunks.baseline: And as if no formalities were needed, they silently stepped aside instead of blocking my way as I came up the stairs.
hunks.sol: As I climbed the stairs, they quietly stepped aside, as though there were no formalities to observe.

hunks.baseline: The enormous iron gate they guarded stood wide open, unlike the last time I’d visited.
hunks.sol: The enormous iron door they guarded stood wide open, unlike the last time I’d visited.

hunks.baseline: And in the deepest part of Qianqing Palace, the Emperor was waiting for me.
hunks.sol: And in the innermost chamber of Qianqing Palace, the Emperor was waiting for me.

hunks.baseline: His tone was gentler than before, his voice warm with welcome.
hunks.sol: His voice was gentler than before, warm with welcome. His eyes were smiling too.

hunks.baseline: And his eyes were smiling.
But even with the welcome of an Emperor known as Iron Blood for his countless purges and ruthless decisions, even before his accession to the throne, I didn’t smile.
hunks.sol: But even faced with such a welcome from the Emperor—a man called Iron Blood for the countless purges and ruthless decisions he’d made since before taking the throne—I didn’t smile.

hunks.baseline: No—to be precise, I couldn’t.
hunks.sol: No. I couldn’t.

hunks.baseline: I hadn’t said it out loud, but apparently I hadn’t managed to hide my bewilderment. It showed in my expression and my eyes.
The Emperor watched me searching for something to say, then gave a quiet laugh and spoke first.
hunks.sol: I hadn’t said it aloud, but my bewilderment must have shown. The Emperor watched me struggle for words, then gave a quiet laugh and spoke first.

hunks.baseline: “You seem rather taken aback. I suppose it’s understandable, given that the Son of Heaven looks like this.”
hunks.sol: “You seem rather taken aback. Understandable, I suppose, when the Son of Heaven looks like this.”

hunks.baseline: He tapped the bandages wrapped around his upper body.
hunks.sol: He tapped the bandages wrapped around his upper body. The faint smile on his lips made his sunken cheeks stand out even more.

hunks.baseline: His cheeks were sunken, made all the more prominent by the faint smile at the corner of his mouth.
“If I may offer you one piece of advice, it’s best to lower your head first at times like this.”
hunks.sol: “A piece of advice: at times like this, lower your head first.”

hunks.baseline: The Emperor looked absurdly gaunt compared to just three days ago. My shock hadn’t eased, but I forced myself to reply calmly.
hunks.sol: He was impossibly gaunt compared to just three days ago. I was still shaken, but I forced myself to reply calmly.

hunks.baseline: “Two. First, you can hide your expression. Second, you buy yourself a little time to think.”
hunks.sol: “Two. You can hide your expression, and you buy yourself a moment to think.”

hunks.baseline: “I see. Since we’re here, I’ll give it a try too.”
hunks.sol: “I see. I might as well try it.”

hunks.baseline: I lowered my head for a moment, then lifted it again before even ten seconds had passed.
hunks.sol: I lowered my head, then lifted it again less than ten seconds later.

hunks.baseline: “I’ve already been found out, so there’s no point trying to hide my expression. But I have to admit, it does give me time to think.”
hunks.sol: “You’ve already seen my expression, so it’s too late to hide that. But the time to think does help.”

hunks.baseline: “I wondered why Your Majesty looks like this. And what the reason might be.”
hunks.sol: “Why Your Majesty looks like this. What caused it.”

hunks.baseline: “You’ve been thinking about something pointless. I simply overexerted myself in that battle.”
hunks.sol: “A waste of thought. I simply overexerted myself in that battle.”

hunks.baseline: The Emperor smiled and waved a hand, but the smile vanished without a trace when he heard my next words.
hunks.sol: The Emperor smiled and waved a hand. The smile vanished when he heard my next words.

hunks.baseline: “So you’ve taken poppy again?”
hunks.sol: “So you’ve been smoking poppy again?”

hunks.baseline: “I was a little slow to notice. Your Majesty’s appearance caught me by surprise, and I didn’t pay attention to the smell around me.”
hunks.sol: “I was slow to notice. The sight of you caught me off guard, and I didn’t pay attention to the smell.”

hunks.baseline: I took a slow breath as I looked at the Emperor’s face, gone rigid. The heavy, peculiar scent drifting into my nose was unmistakably familiar.
hunks.sol: I drew a slow breath as I watched his face go rigid. The strong, peculiar scent that reached me was unmistakably the one I remembered.

hunks.baseline: The Emperor’s voice had sunk low. I thought back to the first time I’d stepped into Qianqing Palace.

hunks.baseline: I remembered the strangely familiar scent I’d sensed from the Emperor I finally met—and the moment I learned the truth through someone who occasionally smoked poppy.
hunks.sol: His voice had dropped. I thought back to the first time I’d entered Qianqing Palace: the strangely familiar scent I’d noticed when I finally met the Emperor, and the moment someone who occasionally smoked poppy had helped me place it.

hunks.baseline: “I can’t imagine how you figured it out. It’s not something you can easily get on the street, and I’d heard Murim practitioners avoid anything that harms the mind and spirit.”
hunks.sol: “I can’t imagine how you figured it out. It isn’t easy to obtain, and I’ve heard Murim practitioners avoid anything that harms the mind and spirit.”

hunks.baseline: “You’re right. They generally do.”
hunks.sol: “You heard right. Murim practitioners generally do.”

hunks.baseline: I added calmly,
“But I hear eunuchs sometimes use it.”
hunks.sol: I added calmly, “But I hear eunuchs sometimes use it.”

hunks.baseline: Whether the cause is psychological or physical, the human mind and body remember it clearly.
Even decades later, after the scars have faded, old wounds still ache. How much worse must it be for eunuchs, who’ve had their most private parts cut off?
hunks.sol: Whether it’s psychological or physical, the mind and body remember. Old wounds can still ache decades later, even after the scars have faded. How much worse must it be for eunuchs, who’ve had their private parts cut off?

hunks.baseline: Hong Jin was no exception.

hunks.baseline: Whenever the pain struck without warning and he couldn’t bear it, he turned to poppy. That was how I’d accidentally learned one of the Emperor’s secrets.
hunks.sol: Hong Jin was no exception. When the pain came without warning and he couldn’t bear it, he turned to poppy. Thanks to him, I’d stumbled onto one of the Emperor’s secrets.

hunks.baseline: “How long have you been using it, and why?”
hunks.sol: “How long have you been using it? And why?”

hunks.baseline: “Well. I don’t see why you need to know.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t see why you need to know.”

hunks.baseline: Before I could say anything, the Emperor gave a bitter smile and gestured toward his own head.
hunks.sol: Before I could respond, the Emperor gave a bitter smile and pointed to his head.

hunks.baseline: “And even if I told you, it wouldn’t change much.”
hunks.sol: “Besides, nothing I say will change much.”

hunks.baseline: He seemed to have already given up. And that gesture had meaning, too.
hunks.sol: He sounded as though he’d already resigned himself to it. That gesture only made it worse.

hunks.baseline: The Emperor moved his dry lips as I stared at him, eyes wide.
hunks.sol: I stared at him, eyes wide, as he parted his dry lips.

hunks.baseline: “That’s right. What you’re thinking.”
hunks.sol: “That’s right. It’s what you’re thinking.”

hunks.baseline: “The Blood Soul Gu. That cursed poison has already reached my very marrow.”
hunks.sol: “The Blood Soul Gu. That cursed poison has reached my very marrow.”

hunks.baseline: The moment my suspicion became certainty, a curse escaped me with a groan.
hunks.sol: My suspicion hardened into certainty, and a curse escaped me like a groan.

hunks.baseline: “Impertinent. To say something so vulgar in front of me, the father of all the people. If Commander Baek were here, he’d have you dragged to the prison at once.”
hunks.sol: “Impertinent. Such vulgar language before the father of all the people? If Commander Baek were here, he’d have you dragged to prison at once.”

hunks.baseline: Someone else might have trembled and begged forgiveness, but I only sighed at the Emperor, who was making a show of frowning.
hunks.sol: Someone else might have trembled and begged forgiveness. I only sighed at the Emperor, who was making a show of frowning.

hunks.baseline: “Have I ever told you I’m good at jokes?”
hunks.sol: “Have I ever told you I’m good at them?”

hunks.baseline: “This is the first I’ve heard of it. And you’re so bad it gives me goose bumps.”
hunks.sol: “This is the first I’ve heard of it. You’re so bad it gives me goose bumps.”

hunks.baseline: “That’s because you’re a dull fellow. Back when I was campaigning on the battlefield, I’d drink and laugh with my men every night. Those were good times.”
hunks.sol: “That’s because you’re a dull fellow. Back when I was campaigning, I’d drink and laugh with my men every night. Those were good times.”

hunks.baseline: I didn’t know who his men had been back then, but they must’ve worked hard to laugh along.
hunks.sol: I didn’t know who those men had been, but they must have worked hard to laugh along.

hunks.baseline: Not that any of that mattered right now.
hunks.sol: Not that it mattered right now.

hunks.baseline: I shook my head at the tactless commander—or rather, Emperor—and asked what I was most curious about.
hunks.sol: I shook my head at the clueless division commander—no, Emperor—and asked what I most wanted to know.

hunks.baseline: The Emperor continued calmly, as though there was nothing left to hide.
hunks.sol: As though there was nothing left to hide, the Emperor continued calmly.

hunks.baseline: “A trusted loyalist did it. By the time I realized, it was already too late.”
hunks.sol: “A loyal servant I trusted did it. By the time I realized, it was too late.”

hunks.baseline: “Who among Your Majesty’s inner circle knows?”
hunks.sol: “Who among Your Majesty’s closest people knows?”

hunks.baseline: “Only two people. Baek Yeon and So Gyo. Though perhaps I should call her the Bow Saint now.”
hunks.sol: “Only two. Baek Yeon and So Gyo. Though perhaps I should call her the Bow Saint now.”

hunks.baseline: The Emperor looked at me and added,
“And here, today, one more person has learned a truth that must never be known.”
hunks.sol: He looked at me and added, “And today, one more person has learned a truth that must never be known.”

hunks.baseline: I understood what he meant at once and clicked my tongue.
hunks.sol: I caught his meaning at once and clicked my tongue.

hunks.baseline: “In that respect, I’m much better off. I can’t disgrace myself like that as Emperor.”
hunks.sol: “Then I’m better off than you. As Emperor, I can’t make such a disgrace of myself.”

hunks.baseline: That was when it happened.
hunks.sol: He gave a soft chuckle. Then, without warning, he coughed.

hunks.baseline: The Emperor, who’d been chuckling softly, suddenly gave a small cough.
His golden sleeve stained red. I looked around, my face hardening at the sudden spitting of blood, but the Emperor shook his head before I could move.
hunks.sol: Red stained his golden sleeve. I looked around, my face hardening at the sight of blood, but the Emperor shook his head before I could move.

hunks.baseline: “If their medicine could’ve treated this, I would’ve sought their help long ago. Why do you think I hid this even from the imperial physicians?”
hunks.sol: “If they could cure this, I’d have done something about it long ago. Why do you think I hid it even from them?”

hunks.baseline: The Emperor gazed at his blood-soaked sleeve and murmured as though to himself.
hunks.sol: The Emperor gazed at his blood-soaked sleeve and murmured as if to himself.

hunks.baseline: “My father and mother. My three elder brothers. And the senior members of the imperial family who worked so faithfully to protect the ancestral shrines and the state… Not one person was spared. They all died.”
hunks.sol: “My father and mother. My three elder brothers. The senior members of the imperial family who worked so faithfully to uphold the ancestral shrines and the state… Not one was spared. None escaped death.”

hunks.baseline: That was right. No one had escaped the Blood Soul Gu’s grasp.
hunks.sol: He was right. No one had escaped the Blood Soul Gu’s grasp.

hunks.baseline: That was why his attempt to set everything right after the coup had come to nothing.

The late Emperor, the Empress, and several direct members of the imperial family, including the Crown Prince, had died one after another. The Fourth Prince who’d started the coup was branded an unfilial son and an unforgivable usurper.
hunks.sol: That was why his attempt to set everything right after the coup had failed. The late Emperor, the Empress, and several direct members of the imperial family, including the Crown Prince, had died one after another. The Fourth Prince who’d started the coup had been branded an unforgivable, unfilial son and a usurper.

hunks.baseline: “I have no regrets left. I took every elixir I could to stay alive, and trained in martial arts until my bones ached, trying to overcome the Blood Soul Gu’s poison. I endured like that for ten years.”
hunks.sol: “I have no regrets left. I took every elixir I could to stay alive and trained in martial arts at a bone-grinding pace to withstand the Blood Soul Gu’s poison. I held on like that for ten years.”

hunks.baseline: At last, I understood.
Why he—the man who held the greatest territory in the world and commanded countless troops—had reached the realm he stood in now.
hunks.sol: At last, I understood why he—the man who held the greatest territory in the world and commanded countless troops—had reached his current realm.

hunks.baseline: “After enduring a winter that lasted more than ten years, spring has finally come. That’s enough for me.”
hunks.sol: “After enduring a winter of more than ten years, spring has finally come. That’s enough for me.”

hunks.baseline: Right now,
a clear smile rested on the Emperor’s lips.
hunks.sol: At that moment, a clear smile rested on the Emperor’s lips.
